Kithlish
KITH-lish
proper noun
A city in the lowland (Shephelah) of Judah, named in the roll of Judah’s inheritance; the name is taken to mean “a man’s wall” or “God separates.”

Biblical Definition

Kithlish is a city in the lowland of Judah, named once in the roll of Judah’s inheritance: “And Cabbon, and Lahmam, and Kithlish” (Jos 15:40). It is among the last towns of a Shephelah cluster and is nowhere else mentioned. The name is taken by some to carry the sense of separation — that God divides and sets apart. However uncertain the etymology, the truth of separation runs through the whole story of the inheritance, for the LORD had separated Israel from the peoples to be a possession unto Himself, and had separated the towns of Canaan from the hand of the Amorite to give them to His people. Every name in this catalogue is a boundary-stone of that separation: this town, and not the Philistine’s; this field, given to Judah, and not left to the heathen. “The LORD hath set apart him that is godly for himself” (Psa 4:3). What God did in the map of Canaan He does in redemption: He separates a people to Himself out of the mass of fallen mankind, marking them off by sovereign grace, and settling them at last in an inheritance incorruptible. Little Kithlish, of which the world knows nothing, was Judah’s by the LORD’s dividing hand; and every soul chosen in Christ is His by the same electing separation, kept for a possession that fadeth not away.

Webster 1828 Definition

A city in the lowland of Judah, named once in the roll of Judah’s inheritance; the name carries the sense of separation.

KITHLISH, a city in the lowland (Shephelah) of Judah.

It is named a single time, among the last towns of a valley cluster.

The name is taken to mean a man’s wall, or God separates.

No narrative is attached to it in Scripture.

Its witness is God’s separating of a people and a portion to Himself.

Key Scripture

Jos 15:40 — "And Cabbon, and Lahmam, and Kithlish,"

Psa 4:3 — "But know that the LORD hath set apart him that is godly for himself: the LORD will hear when I call unto him."

Jos 21:43 — "And the LORD gave unto Israel all the land which he sware to give unto their fathers; and they possessed it, and dwelt therein."

1Pe 1:4 — "To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you,"

Modern Corruption

A city of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it recovers the truth that God separates a people and a portion to Himself by sovereign grace.

expand to see more

Kithlish faces no postmodern redefinition. The truth its name carries answers the levelling spirit that will not have God set any apart, but insists all peoples and all portions are alike, and grace no distinguishing thing.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is separating grace. As the LORD divided the towns of Canaan and gave Kithlish to Judah, so He sets apart the godly for Himself, marking off a people out of fallen mankind for an inheritance incorruptible, reserved in heaven.

Hebrew Roots

An unrecorded lowland town of Judah whose name carries the sense of separation; a witness to God’s setting apart of a people and portion.
